clinician.trajectory_summary: A 20-year-old gravida 2 para 1 live 1 abortion 1 Iranian female presented on postpartum day 1 (November 2023) with sudden onset dyspnea and left hemithorax pain following uncomplicated vaginal delivery at 38+4 weeks gestation. On admission, she was in severe respiratory distress (RR 35, HR 146, O2 sat 88%) with reduced left lung sounds. Physical examination revealed a 1 cm suburethral vaginal lesion. Laboratory evaluation showed markedly elevated β-HCG of 1,254,800 mIU/mL. Chest imaging demonstrated left-sided hemothorax with bilateral pulmonary nodules on HRCT (up to 41 mm right upper lobe, 34 mm left lung) consistent with metastases. Based on the clinical presentation, markedly elevated β-HCG, and radiological evidence of bilateral pulmonary nodules, a diagnosis of pulmonary metastatic choriocarcinoma was established. The patient was referred to oncology and initiated on EMA/CO chemotherapy (etoposide, methotrexate, actinomycin D, cyclophosphamide, vincristine). Serum β-HCG monitoring demonstrated good response to treatment, with β-HCG reduced to 125 mIU/mL after three cycles of chemotherapy. The patient continued her chemotherapy regimen at the time of documentation.
